experience.linkedin_description:
I lead development on Ludwig, a practice-management platform for physiotherapy clinics in Germany and Austria. It is used day to day by 20+ therapists and holds records for more than 10,000 patients.

I built most of it from scratch: architecture, UI, frontend, backend integration, testing, deployment, and everything since. I work directly with the CEO, so requirements reach me as business problems and I turn them into something that works for people who are busy and not technical.

What is in it:
• Clinical documentation and patient records
• Appointment scheduling, recurring bookings and available time-slot calculation
• Resource management, therapist absences and waiting lists
• Statutory health insurance (GKV) invoicing
• A booking wizard practices embed in their own website
• Mobile apps for therapists

Two parts were the hard ones. Multi-tenant architecture, so one deployment serves many practices with their data properly separated. And offline-first sync with conflict handling, because a therapist in a treatment room often has no signal and still needs to write notes, and when two people touch the same record nobody's work should disappear.

I also guide a team of 3-4 engineers on our other products: a business connector, a business-card management platform, and a regional public registry. That means technical direction, code reviews, and unblocking people.

Technologies: Angular 19, Ionic 8, TypeScript, Next.js 16, React 19, Flutter, RxJS, NgRx Signals, Tailwind CSS, Playwright, PDF workflows

experience.linkedin_description:
Three years building web and mobile products for clients in logistics, marketplaces, real estate and field services. I started as a developer and moved into leading a team of 5-10.

Most of my work was backend: system design, APIs and data. I built scalable APIs in Node.js and TypeScript, worked with both SQL and NoSQL through TypeORM, Sequelize and Mongoose, and spent real time getting the database structure right before writing the code that depends on it.

The harder pieces:
• Billing systems and payment gateway integrations
• Large CSV exports that had to stay fast as the data grew
• Asynchronous processing to keep heavy jobs off the request path
• File and media handling with AWS S3 and Cloudinary
• Logging and alerting through AWS SNS, so problems showed up before clients reported them
• GraphQL and Google Maps API integration
• Unit tests with Jest

The products this went into:
• A 3PL logistics and order fulfilment system: inbound and outbound orders, inventory across warehouses, live tracking.
• A heavy equipment marketplace for buying, renting and listing machinery.
• SandSeekers, a real estate platform for the Dubai market with its own CRM. I pulled live feeds from Bayut, Dubizzle and Property Finder and normalised three inconsistent sources into one searchable catalogue.
• 99DPF, a service booking platform on web and mobile, with real-time chat, push notifications and live order status.
• CorporateMerch, a corporate gifting platform with AI-generated designs.
• A data platform that collects and structures millions of property listings.

As team lead I reviewed code, mentored the junior developers, joined client calls to turn vague requirements into something we could build, and planned what shipped when.

Technologies: Node.js, NestJS, TypeScript, React, Angular, Next.js, React Native, PostgreSQL, MongoDB, MariaDB, Redis, TypeORM, Sequelize, Mongoose, GraphQL, AWS (S3, SNS), Cloudinary, Jest, Socket.IO

linkedin_about:
I'm a Full Stack Developer based in Innsbruck, Austria, with 4+ years of experience building web and mobile products.

Right now I lead development on Ludwig, a practice-management platform for physiotherapy clinics. I built most of it from scratch, and it runs day to day for 20+ therapists and more than 10,000 patients in Germany and Austria. I work in a team of 3-4 engineers and I'm involved from planning through to release.

Before this I spent three years at Pikessoft, in teams of 5-10 developers, working across a lot of different products: a 3PL logistics and order fulfilment system, a heavy equipment marketplace, a real estate platform with its own CRM for the Dubai market, a service booking product for web and mobile, and a data platform that collects and structures millions of property listings.

Picking up a new domain is normal for me. Logistics, healthcare, real estate, e-commerce. The business rules change, the engineering doesn't.

I've worked in Agile/Scrum teams throughout, with daily standups, sprint planning and code reviews as part of the routine.
